notes.text: Allow a managed Next.js project to be served in production mode when development-server behavior is not representative.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Reprioritized under the 2026-09-05 owner-first, reusable-experiment direction. Revisit when a reproducible production-only debugging need recurs. Queue existing build presets meanwhile; do not introduce another build scheduler or bypass managed finite verification.

notes.author: agent:codex
notes.text: Reconciliation confirms managed development launch and finite build presets, not a build-then-serve production runtime. Keep this optional later feature; a successful build preset must not be described as production serving.

problem: Some defects and performance characteristics appear only in a Next.js production build. Worktree Switcher currently manages only the dev script, so users must leave the control plane to build and serve the selected worktree manually.

risk.rollback: Revert the project to its development launch profile. Production build artifacts remain confined to the selected worktree and can be removed with the cache-reset action.

scope: Add an explicit per-project Next.js runtime profile: development or production; never infer production mode from NODE_ENV supplied by a user override.
For production mode, run the detected package manager's build script to completion and then start Next.js with the configured stable port using explicit shell-free argument arrays.
Represent building separately from server readiness, stream bounded build logs, propagate human-readable failures, and never start the production server after a failed build.
Require the managed server to be stopped before changing profile or rebuilding, and define whether a valid build may be reused for the same worktree and commit.
Count building and running production mode against the global managed-server/heavy-work capacity policy without disturbing unrelated projects.
title: Build and serve managed Next.js projects in production mode
trigger: Revisit when a reproducible production-only debugging need recurs. Queue existing build presets meanwhile; do not introduce another build scheduler or bypass managed finite verification.
validation: Build and start a Next.js worktree in production mode and verify it serves on the project's stable port with NODE_ENV controlled by the runtime profile.
Verify build failure leaves the project failed but stopped, preserves useful logs, and does not consume a runtime capacity slot indefinitely.
Verify switching to a different worktree never serves a stale production artifact from the previous worktree or commit.
Verify development mode remains unchanged and non-Next.js projects cannot select this profile.
value: Developers and agents can reproduce production-only Next.js behavior while preserving Worktree Switcher's port, worktree, reservation, and process ownership guarantees.
